# SPFx React Toolkit documentation

<!-- Generated by scripts/documentation.cjs. Do not edit. -->

SPFx React Toolkit provides React controls, providers, hooks, typed styles, helpers and services for SharePoint Framework applications. It brings together access to SPFx context, component properties, HTTP clients, PnPjs, themes, permissions and storage. Host-specific providers keep runtime state scoped to each SPFx instance.

Use this documentation to integrate the toolkit into an application, choose APIs for a feature, or contribute to the library. If you already know a symbol's name, go directly to the [alphabetical API catalog](api/INDEX.md).

## Start with your first integration

Follow these guides when adding the toolkit to an existing SPFx project:

1. [Install the package and compatible peers](getting-started/installation.md). Check the host's dependencies, shared React/Fluent/Griffel runtimes and the distinction between declared compatibility and the verified toolchain baseline.
2. [Build a first web part](getting-started/quick-start.md). Follow a complete example that mounts a provider, reads user information through a hook and unmounts the React tree when the web part is disposed.
3. [Choose the provider for your host](getting-started/choosing-a-provider.md). Understand the integration points for web parts, Application Customizers, Field Customizers and ListView Command Sets, including their validation limits.

## Task guides

Controls compose interactions; native Property Pane factories configure the host. Providers connect an actual SPFx instance, hooks expose React-facing state and operations, helpers/styles transform explicit inputs, and services perform I/O with caller-supplied clients outside React. Associated types stay with their capability; the generated catalog discovers their legal imports.

Choose a task guide to understand integration order, application-owned state and verification boundaries. Follow its canonical API links for signatures, defaults, legal imports and associated types. Navigation below is discovered from the source files.

## Develop and verify the toolkit

The [development documentation](development/INDEX.md) covers the npm workspaces, local setup, build/debug workflow, browser fixtures and verification commands. The private SPFx sample consumes the compiled library, so library source changes require a library rebuild and a restart of the app's serve process.

Use the [SharePoint validation procedures](development/sharepoint-validation/INDEX.md) when checking behavior in an authenticated host. They describe setup, one essential boundary checklist and how to record results. Local tests and builds do not establish tenant permissions, Graph consent or actual SharePoint-host behavior.

For documentation changes, follow the [authoring and maintenance guide](development/documentation.md). It explains content ownership, API page structure, generated catalog/README updates and link verification. Source JSDoc supports IntelliSense, while the sample provides observable usage scenarios alongside the written references.


## Getting started

- [Choose a provider](getting-started/choosing-a-provider.md): Choose a provider for the actual initialized SPFx instance, and bind its React tree to that host surface’s lifetime.
- [Install the toolkit and shared peers](getting-started/installation.md): Install the toolkit in the consuming SPFx application and align its shared runtimes with the host. Declared peer ranges and the repository verification baseline are different compatibility claims.
- [Build a first SPFx web part](getting-started/quick-start.md): Mount a complete web part with WebPartShell, wire title metadata and Property Pane settings, then unmount its React tree when SPFx disposes the host.

## Guides

- [Control presentation slots](guides/control-slots.md): Customize named presentation regions with shorthand content or slot objects while preserving the control’s semantics, labels, refs and event wiring.
- [Own grid data and navigation](guides/data-grids.md): Create a typed column suite or render dynamic records, then own sorting, filtering, off-page selection and request state in the application.
- [Persist a single editable region](guides/editing.md): Choose a permitted HTML block and formatting policy, then retain one saved content authority through controlled echoes, edit mode and recovery.
- [Build forms with explicit ownership](guides/forms.md): Choose one form suite and validation owner, compose fields inside a native form, then await persistence before reset or dismissal. Records, drafts and date/time domains require deliberate application policies.
- [Compose helpers and services outside React](guides/helpers-and-services.md): Use explicit inputs and initialized clients to compose transformations and I/O outside React. The caller owns authentication, request policy and service lifetime.
- [Choose and invoke an HTTP client](guides/http-clients.md): Choose the HTTP client for the target resource and distinguish initialization, invocation state, request failure and authorization.
- [Localization](guides/localization.md): Toolkit UI text uses native SPFx localized resources, separated by control/family. The package ships all 50 SharePoint UI cultures listed in [the locale fixture](../tests/fixtures/sharepoint-ui-locales.json): eight resources and 400 AMD files. Canonical JSON dictionaries are validated for exact keys, nonblank text, template parameters, plural categories and calendar arrays during the library build. Translations have structural and sampled semantic review; they are not a native-speaker certification for every culture.
- [Read host metadata and diagnose behavior](guides/metadata-and-diagnostics.md): Use provider hooks for live host integration and explicit helpers for supplied PageContext snapshots. Distinguish UI culture, regional formatting, site correlation, measurement and asynchronous SDK metadata.
- [Package imports and tree shaking](guides/package-imports.md): Choose supported package entry points while preserving public aliases, shared runtime identities and explicit PnP feature registrations.
- [Plan permissions and API prechecks](guides/permissions.md): Choose a permission check for the protected resource and treat the result as advisory evidence before the server authorizes a request.
- [Select and persist SharePoint references](guides/pickers.md): Choose a discovery source, keep complete saved identities distinct from their resolved display subset, and treat navigation, accepted scope and remote writes as separate decisions.
- [Choosing and composing React controls](guides/react-controls.md): Compose controls around explicit state, native form ownership and host lifetimes. Choose presentation independently of persistence and verify real-host behavior separately.
- [Use stable callbacks and committed values](guides/react-utilities.md): Keep callback identity stable after commit while reading current state, and distinguish render-time behavior from retained event callbacks.
- [Choose a storage scope](guides/storage.md): Choose storage by lifetime, sharing and permissions, then define read, write and failure ownership.
- [Compose typed styles](guides/styling.md): Compose typed descriptors inside React through the host renderer and theme, with deliberate precedence and browser verification.
